title: Bidirectional A* in San Francisco: Real-Map Routing ⚡
description: Watch Bidirectional A* compute an optimal route between two Mission District landmarks using two simultaneous A* frontiers (start→goal and goal→start). The moment the frontiers meet, we stitch the path—faster than classic A* on large road graphs.
ig_caption:
Bidirectional A* on Real Maps: The Ultimate Pathfinding Algorithm — how autonomous vehicles and routing AI calculate optimal routes in milliseconds ⚡

You’re not watching one search—you’re watching two. Bidirectional A* runs A* from the start and from the goal at the same time, each using a heuristic to expand the most promising streets first.

🔁 What happens under the hood?
1) Forward A*: expands nodes using g(n)+h(n) from the start.
2) Backward A*: expands nodes using g(n)+h(n) from the goal.
3) The speed-up: when the two frontiers meet, we combine parent links to reconstruct the shortest path.

✅ Takeaway: on big real-world road graphs, splitting the search can dramatically cut expansions—especially when the heuristic is informative.

🤔 Debate question: Should routing AI always use bidirectional search, or only when the map graph is “large enough” to justify the extra bookkeeping?
